cohort: The study included 640 female participants within the first year following delivery, recruited from obstetric clinics in two hospitals in Shenzhen, China.
finding: The study revealed a robust correlation between pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in postpartum women and compromised sexual function, quality of life, and psychological health, with symptomatic POP and longer POP duration being associated with worse outcomes.
cross-section timing: within the first year following delivery
